summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Dominica documents: IMF Article IV reports 2025 and 2026, twelve volumes of the recurrent/budget estimates (2013/14-2025/26), the four CBI regulations (S.R.O. 37/2014, 38/2016, 23/2017, 1/2024), and the 2024 regional Memorandum of Agreement and OECS release. Adds every column of CBI revenue, balances excluding CBI, BOP CBI inflows and VRF/DRF figures from the IMF tables; CBI revenue by item and every column from the estimates; the CBI Unit expenditure programme (incl. object 354 marketing and due diligence) by object and column; CBI shares of revenue and recurrent expenditure (charts and image tables, OCR); established CBI posts; and all fees and contributions in the regulations as terms. One new indicator is proposed.

observations.location: PDF p. 42, Annex (implementation of past advice), "CBI Revenue Allocation"
observations.quote: decreased modestly to 1.0 percent of GDP as of March
observations.notes: Two-column annex table; the sentence reads "VRF balances decreased modestly to 1.0 percent of GDP as of March 2025." Balance of the Disaster Vulnerability Risk and Resilience Fund (VRF), saved from CBI revenue (DSA footnote 6, p. 72: "saving a small part of CBI to its VRF (1.0 percent of GDP, in total)"); the government withdrew funds after a weather shock. P. 14 gives the "current level of 1 percent of GDP".

observations.location: PDF p. 13, para 8
observations.quote: requiring the accumulation of 12 percent of GDP (at a rate of 1.5 percent
observations.notes: Target size of the VRF under the Disaster Resilience Strategy (Pillar 2 of the fiscal framework); continues on p. 14 "per year) in a ND contingency fund from its current level of 1 percent of GDP". The VRF is funded from CBI revenue (p. 72, footnote 6).

observations.location: PDF p. 13, para 8
observations.quote: requiring the accumulation of 12 percent of GDP (at a rate of 1.5 percent
observations.notes: Planned annual accumulation in the VRF ("per year", p. 14). The DSA (p. 72, footnote 6) says the government saves part of CBI in the VRF but not at this frequency or magnitude ("1½ percent of GDP/annually").

observations.location: PDF p. 42, Annex (implementation of past advice), "CBI Revenue Allocation"
observations.quote: The Debt Repayment Fund was established in April 2023 with a target capitalization of 1.3 percent of GDP.
observations.notes: Target capitalisation of the Debt Repayment Fund (DRF), funded from CBI flows (see the 2024 Article IV). Establishment in April 2023 is already an event.

observations.location: PDF p. 14, para 9
observations.quote: VRF balances would rise to 12 percent of GDP by 2032
observations.notes: Under the staff-recommended stronger consolidation path (Scenario 2), not the baseline. Annex IV (p. 49) repeats: fully capitalizes the VRF to 12 percent of GDP by 2032.

observations.location: PDF p. 49, Annex IV para 3
observations.quote: fully capitalizes the VRF to the targeted 12 percent of GDP by 2032 as opposed to remaining fixed at 1 percent of GDP under the baseline
observations.notes: Baseline projection: the VRF stays at 1 percent of GDP (to 2032).

events.title: CBI Amendment Regulations 2016: family government fees and wider dependant ages
events.description: S.R.O. 38 of 2016 raised the age limits for student children and unmarried daughters as dependants from 25 to 28, lowered the age for parents and grandparents from 65 to 55, introduced family government fees on the real-estate route (US$75,000 for up to four, US$100,000 for up to six), cut the fee for other adult dependants to US$25,000 and the child registration fee to US$2,000.
events.quote: These Regulations shall come into force on the 1st day of December, 2016.

events.title: Dominica signs the regional Memorandum of Agreement on CBI programmes
events.description: Prime Minister Roosevelt Skerrit signed the MOA on 20 March 2024 (the other four signature dates are partly illegible in the scan). Signatories agree a common US$200,000 minimum by 30 June 2024, information sharing through a JRCC portal, disclosure of CBI receipts and their use to Parliaments, independent audits, a regional competent authority by 30 June 2024, post-approval due diligence and passport retrieval, and common rules banning "visa-free access" marketing and passport images.
events.location: PDF p. 6 (scan, OCR), signature block, Party B

events.title: Interim Regulatory Commission for CBI announced
events.description: The OECS release says participating governments will soon appoint a 7-member Interim Regulatory Commission (one member from each of the five CBI countries, the OECS Commission and the ECCB) pending legislation for a regional regulator; discounting below the agreed minimum is declared illegal.
events.quote: participating Governments will soon appoint an Interim Regulatory Commission pending the enactment of enabling legislation for the regional regulator.
